summary: echo prints text. A redirect sends a command's output into a file: > replaces the file, >> adds to the end, and 2> captures error messages.
notes: Quotes keep a sentence together as one piece of text and protect characters like ! and ? from the shell.
> creates the file if it does not exist, so you do not need touch first.
ls missing.txt 2> errors.txt prints nothing on screen because the error went into errors.txt.
pitfall: Using > when you meant >> erases the file. After echo "Quiz moved to Tuesday." > reminders.txt, the first two reminders are gone and there is no undo.
